##### 2. Test Result Checks

For each test case several checks must be performed to determine whether a case has a successful or failed
completion. The following table describes the different result check categories.

**Check Category** **Description**
**HTTP Headers** Test cases of this category validate HTTP response and request
headers. During such a test must be checked, if all required headers are
contained and if the content is correct in the context.

Minimum acceptance criteria in all responses:

                      - “Content-Type” or ”Content-Type” with charset-header
                      - “ETag” header

Minimum acceptance criteria in all requests:

                      - “Accept” header
                      - “Authorization” header

**Status Codes** A KNX IoT 3[rd] Party Server must use appropriate HTTP status codes in
every response. The concrete code differs from endpoint to endpoint.
Tests of this category verify that an endpoint responds with the correct
code to given input data.

The KNX IoT 3[rd] Party API specifies several status codes as mandatory.
Only mandatory status codes will be tested in this specification.

**JSON Conformance** Tests of this category validate the syntactically correctness of JSON
responses. To achieve that all responses are structured according to
the data model, every response is validated against JSON schemas.
This assures that:

                      - The content is a well-formed JSON object
                      - Data members, nested fields and data types are correct
                      - Conformance to JSON:API is ensured by using the KNX IoT 3[rd]
Party API schemas, which are based on JSON:API schemas

The correctness of the content of the response bodies with regard to
the project loaded in the KNX IoT 3rd Party API Server is not part of
the KNX Conformity Assessment.
This applies throughout the entire test specification.

**Semantic State** Semantic State tests validate the state of the data model.
This includes a semantical analysis of the JSON responses. Response
data correspond to the specified test data (given by the ETS project).

The details are described in every test case individually. Examples for
tests are:

                      - The state does not change after GET requests.
                      - After POST/PUT/DELETE requests the state changed as
expected.

##### 3. Test Categories

All test cases are divided into four test categories, to cover the different aspects and ensure a correct
behavior of a KNX 3[rd] Party API implementation.

  - Static test cases: Test cases related to the project structure.

  - Dynamic test cases: Test cases related to datapoint values, runtime tests, project
specific.

  - Subscription test cases: Test cases related to the gateway communication (WebSockets,
HTTP Callback Subscriptions), not project specific.

  - Security test cases: Test cases related to the authorization procedure (OAuth), not
project specific.

##### 4. Test Scenarios

For each test category a set of test case scenarios is defined, which shall be used to test some aspects of the
API. Every endpoint is tested within several scenarios. Which scenarios can be applied to an endpoint is
individual. If a scenario can be applied, one or more test cases are derived.

All test case descriptions shall contain references to the scenarios described in the following tables.

##### 5. Test Case Specifications

###### 5.1. Locations

_5.1.1. GET /sites_
5.1.1.1. Positive result, expect child items

**Test ID** 5.1.1.1

**Endpoint** 6.1 GET /sites

**Test scenarios** 1.1.1 Positive Tests - Only required parameters

**Description** Request all available root locations from gateway. The test projects contain
none, one or more sites and buildings as root locations. All root locations
contain child locations and location functions.

**Expectation** The expected response shall provide all sites and/or buildings with the links to
the child locations and the links to the location functions. The endpoint shall
contain only root locations.
In case of none, a JSON API conforming empty payload shall be returned,
including

                      - a meta member with a collection member with number size and total
members, all 0.
                      - An empty data member data :[] for collections
**Specification reference** 3_10_4 KNX IoT 3rd Party API v0.1, 1.3.2.2 Locations

**Setup** Root locations with child locations and locations functions are available in the
ETS test project.
A valid API access token is available.

**Parameters** **HTTP headers:**
Accept: application/vnd.api+json
Authorization: “Bearer <valid access token>”

**URL path / parameters:**
/sites

**Request body:**
n/a

**Expected result** **HTTP headers:**
Content-type: application/vnd.api+json
ETag: “<resource identifier>”

**HTTP status code:**
200

**Response body:**

5.1.1.2. Positive result, check parent location link, expect no parent location

**Test ID** 5.1.1.2
**Endpoint** 6.1 GET /sites

**Test scenarios** 1.1.1 Positive tests - Only required parameters

**Description** This test case consists of two HTTP requests. The first request fetches all root
locations which are present in the project. The second request fetches the
parent location with the given URL from the “parentLocation” relation.

**Expectation** The expected result of the two requests are:

1. The “relationships” member contains always a child item

“parentLocation”, which provides an URL.
2. The second request made with the URL from the first request, returns

a “data” member with null as it’s value.

**Specification reference** 3_10_4 KNX IoT 3rd Party API v0.1, 1.3.2.2 Locations

**Setup** KNX IoT 3[rd] Party API Certification ETS test project is loaded to the gateway.
Root locations with child locations and locations functions are available in the
ETS test project.
A valid API access token is available.

**Parameters** **HTTP headers:**
**Step 1** Accept: application/vnd.api+json

Authorization: “Bearer <valid access token>”

**URL path / parameters:**
/sites

**Request body:**
n/a

**Expected result** **HTTP headers:**
**Step 1** Content-type: application/vnd.api+json

ETag: “<resource identifier>”

**HTTP status code:**
200

**Response body:**

**Description** Requests basic information about the KNX IoT 3[rd] Party API Server. This test
checks whether the server returns a well-formed JSON response. The response
is validated with the JSON schema.

**Expectation** The expected response shall contain at least the “api” member. The member
“supportedversions” may be available (also as an empty array).
If the “links” member is present it must contain all mandatory and any
supported (optional) features.

If the “supportedversions” is available as a non-empty array, it must also
contain the members “base” and “version”.

n/a

**Expected result** **HTTP headers:**
Content-type: application/json
ETag: “<resource identifier>”

**HTTP status code:**
200

**Response body:**
```
            <JSON with information about the API>

```

_5.6.4. PATCH /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}_

5.6.4.1. Positive result; Update URL

**Test ID** 5.6.4.1
**Endpoint** 7.4 PATCH /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}

**Test scenarios** 1.1.1 Positive Tests - Only required parameters

**Description** This test checks, if the server handles updates to HTTP based subscriptions
correct. The following steps are executed:

1. Get a datapoint by requesting /datapoints.
2. Create the subscription by calling POST /subscriptions.
3. Set the value through the endpoint PUT /datapoints/values.
4. Wait for a corresponding KNX telegram and check it for correct value

and type information (Not applicable if no actual KNX installation is
used).
5. Wait to receive a notification on the in step 2 posted URL.
6. Update the URL by calling PATCH /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}
7. Set the value through the endpoint PUT /datapoints/values.
8. Wait for a corresponding KNX telegram and check it for correct value

and type information (Not applicable if no actual KNX installation is
used).
9. Wait to receive a notification on the in step 6 updated URL.

**Expectation** The request returns with HTTP status code 200. The JSON body is a wellformed JSON response and validates against the JSON schema without errors.
After step 6 the server updated the callback URL correctly. Events are sent to
the new URL from this point on.

ETag: “<resource identifier>”

**Description** This test case checks correct handling of websocket write commands by the
KNX IoT 3[rd] Party Server. A value gets written to an existing datapoint.

_5.7.5. Unsubscribe-Command_

5.7.5.1. Positive Result; Check notification

**Test ID** 5.7.5.1.
**Endpoint** 7.7 GET /messaging/ws

**Test scenarios** 1.1.1 Positive Tests - Only required parameters

**Description** The test ensures correct behavior of a deleted HTTP based subscription
callback. To achieve this, following steps will be executed:

1. Get a datapoint by requesting GET /datapoints.
2. Create the subscription sending a subscribe command.
3. Set a value by sending a write command on the websocket.
4. Wait to receive a notification event message on the websocket.
5. Delete the subscription by sending an unsubscribe command.

5.7.5.2. Positive result; Check notification after connection terminated

**Test ID** 5.7.5.2.
**Endpoint** 7.7 GET /messaging/ws

**Test scenarios** 1.1.1 Positive Tests - Only required parameters

**Description** The test ensures correct deletion of a websocket based subscription, when the
websocket connection is terminated.

1. Get a datapoint by requesting /datapoints.
2. Create the subscription by sending a subscribe command.
3. Set a value by sending a write command on the websocket.
4. Wait for a corresponding KNX telegram and check it for correct value

and type information (Not applicable if no actual KNX installation is
used).
5. Wait to receive a notification event message on the websocket.
6. Close the websocket connection.
7. Start the websocket connection.
8. Set a value by sending a write command on the websocket.
9. No new event notification arrives.

**Expectation** All requests execute successfully.

200

```
            <JSON with list of datapoints>
```

5.7.5.3. Positive result; Check lifetime

**Test ID** 5.7.5.3.
**Endpoint** 7.7 GET /messaging/ws

**Test scenarios** 1.1.1 Positive Tests - Only required parameters

**Description** The test ensures correct deletion of a websocket based subscription, after the
lifetime has ended.

1. Get a datapoint by requesting /datapoints.
2. Create the subscription by sending a subscribe command. Set the

lifetime to 30 seconds.
3. Set a value by sending a write command on the websocket.
4. Wait for a corresponding KNX telegram and check it for correct value

and type information (Not applicable if no actual KNX installation is
used).
5. Wait to receive a notification event message on the websocket.
6. Wait 30 seconds.
7. Set a value by sending a write command on the websocket.
8. No new event notification arrives.

**Expectation** All requests execute successfully.

###### 5.8. Discovery

_5.8.1. DNS-SD & mDNS_

5.8.1.1. Positive result; LAN environment

**Test ID** 5.8.1.1.
**Test scenarios**
**Description** This test ensures the ability of the KNX IoT 3[rd] Party Server to be found in a
local network via DNS-SD and mDNS. The parameter “_knx._tcp” will be used
to find all TCP based KNX Services in the local network.

**Expectation** DNS-SD and mDNS queries result in an IP address and port. By using this IP
information HTTP GET calls to the endpoints ./well-known/knx and /node can
be executed. The returned node ID must match the preconfigured node ID.

**Specification reference** 3_10_4 KNX IoT 3rd Party API v0.1; 1.3.3 Discovery

**Setup** Following information must be preconfigured in the test tool:

                      - The manufacturer name or ID
                      - The serial number of the tested KNX IoT 3[rd] Party Server instance
                      - The node ID
                      - Valid server credentials

**Step 1** Execute a DNS-SD query with “_knx._tcp.local” as parameter.

**Expected result** - The response is a list of DNS records with at least one SRV record.
**Step 1** - One of the SRV records must contain the correct host name.

                      - The host name consists of the preconfigured manufacturer
information and serial number.
                      - The Manufacturer information must be the manufacturer name as
specified in KIM, clause "KNX Manufacturer Content”. Alternatively,
the KNX manufacturer ID can be used.
                      - The serial number must be the same as the device serial number, but
only capital letters are allowed.
                      - Other DNS records will not be evaluated in this test.

**Step 2** Execute a mDNS query with the result from step one (host name) as

parameter.

**Expected result** - The response is a list of DNS records with at least one A or AAAA
**Step 2** record.

                      - The records must contain at least IP address and port.
                      - Other DNS records will not be evaluated in this test.

**Step 3** Send a HTTP GET request to <ip-address>:<port>/well-known/knx .

**Expected result** - The request returns with HTTP status code 200.
**Step 3** - The JSON body validates against the JSON schema without errors.

**Step 4** Send a HTTP GET request to <ip-address>:<port>/node .

|**Expectation**|DNS-SD and mDNS queries result in an IP address and port. By using this IP<br>information HTTP GET calls to the endpoints ./well-known/knx and /node can<br>be executed. The returned node ID must match the preconfigured node ID.|

5.8.1.2. Positive result; LAN environment with subcategory

**Test ID** 5.8.1.2.
**Test scenarios**
**Description** This test ensures the ability of the KNX IoT 3[rd] Party Server to be found in a
local network via DNS-SD and mDNS. The parameter “_restapi._sub._knx._tcp”
will be used to only find KNX REST APIs in the local network.

**Expectation** DNS-SD and mDNS queries result in an IP address and port. By using this IP
information HTTP GET calls to the endpoints ./well-known/knx and /node can
be executed. The returned node ID must match the preconfigured node ID.

**Specification reference** 3_10_4 KNX IoT 3rd Party API v0.1; 1.3.3 Discovery

**Setup** Following information must be preconfigured in the test tool:

                      - The manufacturer name or ID
                      - The serial number of the tested KNX IoT 3[rd] Party Server instance
                      - The node ID
                      - A valid access token

**Step 1** Execute a DNS-SD query with “_restapi._sub._knx._tcp” as parameter.

**Expected result** - The response is a list of DNS records with at least one SRV record.
**Step 1** - One of the SRV records must contain the correct host name.

                      - The host name consists of the preconfigured manufacturer
information and serial number.
                      - The Manufacturer information must be the manufacturer name as
specified in KIM, clause "KNX Manufacturer Content”. Alternatively,
the KNX manufacturer ID can be used.
                      - The serial number must be the same as the device serial number, but
only capital letters are allowed.
                      - Other DNS records will not be evaluated in this test.

**Step 2** Execute a mDNS query with the result from step one (host name) as

parameter.

**Expected result** - The response is a list of DNS records with at least one A or AAAA
**Step 2** record.

                      - The records must contain at least IP address and port.
                      - Other DNS records will not be evaluated in this test.

**Step 3** Send a HTTP GET request to <ip-address>:<port>/well-known/knx .

**Expected result** - The request returns with HTTP status code 200.
**Step 3** - The JSON body validates against the JSON schema without errors.

**Step 4** Send a HTTP GET request to <ip-address>:<port>/node .

**Expected result** - The request returns with HTTP status code 200.
**Step 4** - The JSON body validates against the JSON schema without errors.

                      - The ID of the returned item is the same as the preconfigured node ID.

returns. To achieve this, following steps are executed:

for authorization with the grant type “authorization code”.
2. Wait for the token to be expired.
3. Call the endpoint GET /datapoints.

**Expectation** 1. The request is successful (HTTP status code 200) and returns a valid

JSON body, containing an access token. The form and structure of the
access token itself will not be further checked.
2. The time passes.
3. No access to the endpoint is possible. The endpoint returns HTTP

status code 401 and an error response.

Server.
A valid client ID is provided.
An authorization code with permissions to the scopes “read”, “write” and
“manage” is provided.

Content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

POST /oauth/access

```
             "redirect_uri": "<redirectUri>"
            }

```

**Step 1** Content-type: application/json

**HTTP status code:**
200

**Response body:**
```
            {

```

done by comparing the fingerprints of the certificates.
